newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-ELBER MAY UPSTAGE KLINSMANN IN KEY CLASH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-ELBER MAY UPSTAGE KLINSMANN IN KEY CLASH.

text.p: It takes a big player to attract more attention than Juergen Klinsmann when the Bayern Munich striker is returning to the club where he made his name.

But more eyes are likely to be on VfB Stuttgart's Brazilian forward Giovane Elber than on Germany's national team captain when Bayern travel to Stuttgart for Sunday's top-of-the-table Bundesliga clash.
While Klinsmann has struggled to score consistently in domestic football this season, Elber has proved that he has the kind of outrageous skill which can turn a match in a few seconds.

His 10 goals in the first 15 games have been crucial to Stuttgart's successful first half of the season. His striking partnership with Euro 96 forward Fredi Bobic, who has also 10 goals to his name, is the most successful in Germany.
Ironically, Elber wanted to go to Bayern last season when Stuttgart were not making a major impact in the Bundesliga. But VfB turned down the Bavarians' offer.
There are suggestions again that he might still be heading to Germany's richest club next season. The Brazilian is certainly not ruling out a move to a more glamorous club.
"There are enough offers," Elber said. "From abroad -- also interesting offers. I will make a decision about my future during the winter break.
"I am not one of those comfortable footballers who plays for the same club for 10 years and fetch their money.
"I want to achieve a great deal in football and when I return to Brazil I want to be able to sit down and think 'Firstly I played for Grasshopper Zurich and then Stuttgart and it went up and up."
Elber came to Stuttgart from Grasshopper in 1994. He has certainly earned his money, scoring 34 times in 71 league matches.

But the Brazilian knows that he needs to play for a club that has a high profile all the time if he is to make a career in the national team, especially with the 1998 World Cup finals in France less than two years away.
Before this season Stuttgart had struggled to make an impact in the Bundesliga since they won the title in 1992.
But Elber said: "It is a different situation now. We could win the title or German Cup and get into the UEFA Cup. The news will get around in Brazil."
In Sunday's clash, Klinsmann will be returning to the club where he made his name in Germany before moving abroad to Internazionale, Monaco and Tottenham.
He reached the UEFA Cup final with Stuttgart and still has friends and fans in the city. But there is a good chance that many of them will be cheering for Elber on Sunday.
